title: Moment
description: A selectable, semantically coherent source range with content, quality, rights, and candidate-role features (PRD §5 object table, REQ-018). Immutable per source-index version. The assembled set is the Moment Graph. Every REQ-018 field below is REQUIRED — a field with nothing to say carries an explicit null plus a stated reason rather than being absent, so 'we did not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' stay distinguishable. Produced by DETERMINISTIC segmentation (decisions.md D-31: speaker-turn × shot-boundary intersection, 3–30 s); a model may enrich narrative-function tags only, and never decides the boundaries.

changelog.reason: Initial v1. Carries the per-Moment transcript embedding inline (decisions.md D-22) so Phase 3's retrieval reads stored vectors in pure TypeScript and never shells out to Python for the corpus side. Records segmentation provenance so D-31's 'segmentation is never model-driven' is auditable from the artefact, not just asserted in the spec.

sourceIndexId.description: The SourceIndex revision this Moment was derived from. Moments are immutable per source-index version (PRD §5), so a re-index produces new Moments rather than mutating these.

sourceRange.description: REQ-018's 'exact source range'. Validated against the asset's preflighted duration by `range-check.ts` — the single implementation, run by `cutdown index` over every generated Moment. This is the mechanism behind the 'zero invalid source ranges' Phase 0 exit criterion.

durationSeconds.description: Convenience projection of sourceRange for human reading and for the D-31 3–30 s granularity assertion. NOT authoritative — sourceRange's integer ticks are. Never used for arithmetic that feeds a render.

segmentation.title: SegmentationProvenance
segmentation.description: How this Moment's boundaries were chosen. decisions.md D-31 fixes deterministic segmentation and forbids model-driven boundaries; recording the method and the contributing boundary IDs is what makes that rule checkable against a produced artefact rather than only against the code.

method.description: A `const`, not an enum: at Phase 0 there is exactly one sanctioned method, and adding a second is a deliberate schema change reviewed against D-31.

granularityBounds.title: GranularityBounds
granularityBounds.description: The 3–30 s target window in force when this Moment was cut (D-31). Recorded per Moment so retuning granularity against real footage is visible in the data.

transcript.title: MomentTranscript
transcript.description: REQ-018's 'transcript' for this range. Verbatim and display text are kept apart for the same reason as in SourceIndex: the deterministic quotation gate (D-37 — quote token order and speaker identity) tokenises the VERBATIM side, so a cleaned caption can never launder a misquote past it.

lowConfidenceWordCount.description: How many words fell below the D-28 confidence threshold. A Moment full of low-confidence words is a poor quotation candidate, and the critic surfaces that.

visualSummary.description: REQ-018's 'visual summary'. Null-with-reason when the VLM sub-stage was skipped (e.g. `--no-vlm` before the D-21 spend ceiling is set) — NEVER a fabricated description.

label.description: The corrected name if one exists, otherwise the inferred positional label.

isCorrected.description: Whether `label` came from a human correction. The editorial gate treats an UNCORRECTED label as an unverified speaker identity.

source.description: Which modality asserted it — an on-screen price read by OCR and a spoken price are different evidence.

energyCues.description: REQ-018's 'emotion or energy cues'. Sourced from the REQ-015 audio-event track, so REQ-015's rule rides along: volume alone is never emotional importance, and `audioEventIds` names the classifier events that justified the cue.

technicalQuality.title: MomentQuality
technicalQuality.description: REQ-018's 'technical quality' rollup for this range, projected from the SourceIndex's REQ-014 flags. `usable` is advisory only — an unusable-looking Moment is still offered to the editorial stage with its reasons attached, because the human, not the score, decides.

rights.title: MomentRights
rights.description: REQ-018's 'rights flags', inherited from the owning SourceAsset. Inherited rather than restated: a Moment cannot be more permissively licensed than the footage it is cut from, and duplicating the full record would let the two drift.

candidateNarrativeFunctions.description: REQ-018's 'possible narrative functions' — CANDIDATES, plural and non-exclusive. The story planner chooses; this list only says what the Moment could serve. Optional LLM enrichment (D-31) may populate it, which is the one model contribution to a Moment and never touches its boundaries.

source.description: `model` entries are advisory evidence (D-37) and can never become a blocking signal.

sourceDependencies.description: REQ-018's 'source dependencies': other Moments this one needs in order to make sense — a payoff that is meaningless without its setup, an answer without its question. The story planner uses these to avoid cutting a Moment loose from the context that makes it true, which is also what the deterministic 'required context' editorial gate (D-37) checks.

oneOf.title: MomentEmbedding
oneOf.description: Transcript-text embedding computed during Phase 2 Moment extraction (decisions.md D-22: bge-small-en-v1.5, 384 dims, local). Stored ON the Moment so Phase 3's retrieval does brute-force cosine in pure TypeScript over vectors already on disk — the Stage B move to pgvector is then a re-embed, not a redesign. REQ-017's frame/clip embeddings are deliberately out of Phase 0 scope.

dimensions.description: Capped at 2000: tech-spec §9.2 notes pgvector index types cap around that, so an embedding model chosen now cannot make the Stage B migration impossible.

NullableText.title: NullableText
NullableText.description: Text that may legitimately be unavailable, carrying the REASON it is unavailable. This shape is why the Phase 2 acceptance criterion 'every Moment field populated or explicitly null-with-reason' is schema-enforceable rather than a review convention.

absentReason.description: Non-null exactly when `value` is null. Enforced by the assembler (the subset forbids if/then/else) and asserted by fixture.
